title: JANUS Linear A v0.7 dual-implementation reconciliation
purpose: Reconcile two independently implemented v0.7 local formula/neighborhood analyses that consume the same authoritative v0.6.2 typed-token baseline but use materially different partition, masking, null, representation, and multiplicity strategies.

shared_baseline.reason_external_independence_false: Both implementations use the same frozen transcription corpus and inherit the same typed-token ontology. Their agreement is implementation-level convergence, not external corpus replication.

implementation_A_screen_confirm_mask_geo.label: V0_7_A

method.known_control_treatment: Known control semantic identities become fixed MASK positions in novelty channel so geometry is preserved and synthetic adjacency is not created.
method.HT_partitioning: Deterministic 3/5 screen and 2/5 confirm split by document hash.
null_preserves: semantic-token count and semantic identity multiset per document
method.multiplicity: Screen is exploratory; confirmation and replication use Bonferroni over evaluable locked motifs.

strengths: Independent HT screen and confirmation partitions separate candidate generation from internal confirmation.
Known controls are masked while preserving their positions, preventing geometry artifacts caused by deletion.
Non-evaluability is kept distinct from statistical replication failure.
limitations: Uses one principal relation-destroying null family rather than multiple complementary structural nulls.
Novelty-masked local motif ontology had zero screen-eligible motifs, so it does not test rarer or longer higher-order motifs.

implementation_B_word_only_triple_null.label: V0_7_B

method.known_control_treatment: Removal-only pre-score exclusion from new semantic endpoint hashing/scoring.
method.multiplicity: Candidate must pass max-T family-wise error control under all three discovery nulls; replication is locked-direction with Bonferroni across selected relations x three nulls.

strengths: Uses a single full-word representation, avoiding word/suffix duplicate evidence.
Requires simultaneous survival under three destructive null families with max-T family-wise error control.
Does not consult non-HT data when HT discovery selects zero candidates.
limitations: Uses all HT as one discovery partition and therefore lacks implementation A's independent within-HT confirmation partition.
Known controls are deleted from endpoint eligibility rather than represented as fixed MASK geometry, so candidate geometry differs from implementation A.

reconciliation.reason_intermediate_candidate_set_agreem: The implementations define different motif families, known-control geometry, null families, partition chains, endpoint eligibility, and multiplicity rules. Their intermediate candidate sets are not expected to coincide.
reconciliation.known_control_consistency: Implementation A independently confirms one known-control local adjacency inside disjoint HT partitions; implementation B's stricter novelty-oriented triple-null family does not promote any relation. These facts are compatible because the target families and known-control treatment differ.
reconciliation.highest_admissible_statement: Two materially different v0.7 implementations consuming the same typed corpus independently converge on no new cross-region local formula/neighborhood survivor. One implementation internally confirms a known-control HT motif; the other selects zero relations under stricter triple-null FWER. This is implementation-level convergence on the negative novelty claim, not external corpus replication.

methodological_connection_candidate.name: INDEPENDENT_IMPLEMENTATIONS_CAN_AGREE_ON_CLAIM_CEILING_WHILE_DISAGREEING_ON_INTERMEDIATE_CANDIDATES
methodological_connection_candidate.statement: When independently implemented analyses use different nulls, partitions, geometry preservation, and hypothesis families, agreement at the final claim ceiling can be scientifically meaningful even if the intermediate candidate sets differ.
what_it_gives: reduces dependence of the final novelty conclusion on a single implementation choice
separates implementation robustness from external-data replication
makes disagreements diagnostically useful instead of forcing artificial candidate-level consensus
methodological_connection_candidate.generalization_gate: Require analogous implementation-level convergence in at least one additional JANUS research domain before promotion to a general cross-domain Connection.

roadmap_effect.next: v0.8 higher-order typed motifs / neighborhood-role specialization
v0.8_design_requirements: preserve known controls as fixed MASK geometry where relation geometry would otherwise be changed
retain disjoint HT_SCREEN and HT_CONFIRM before non-HT replication
add at least one complementary structure-preserving null beyond the single document identity shuffle
test higher-order families uniformly rather than privileging v0.7 near-signals
preserve post-score semantic reveal and family-wise correction
do not lower thresholds because both v0.7 novelty analyses are negative
roadmap_effect.external_replication_blocker: Independent transcription/parser source remains required before any future structural survivor can be called externally replicated.
